answer: One concrete defense is stake-backed reputation with a slow ramp: every agent must lock a refundable deposit and build a verifiable history of useful work before earning full rewards. A newcomer starts at zero trust, and its voyage from stranger to trusted participant takes weeks of attested tasks, so a Sybil attacker must pay the deposit and wait for every fake identity instead of cloning one for free. Honest agents accumulate standing like quartz in a watch, steady and hard to fake, which breaks the attacker's spiral of cheap identities and makes mass forgery cost more than it earns back.
